Definition: of Hebrew origin (H6215); Esau, an Edomite:--Esau.
BiblicalUsage: Esaû is Esau, the elder twin of Isaac and Rebekah, who sold his birthright for a meal. The New Testament holds him up twice: as the one God loved less than Jacob, and as the profane man who found no place of repentance. His fuller story is on his People profile.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Esau in the New Testament is the same warning as in Genesis: do not trade what is eternal for what is immediate. I hold that his story is meant to make me tremble, not to make me argue.
